newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FORECAST - GIO's half year earnings expected firmer.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - GIO's half year earnings expected firmer.

text.p: Insurance group GIO Australia Holdings Ltd is expected to report a slightly stronger half-year net profit on Wednesday, with most analysts saying a good performance from the investment unit should support earnings.

A survey of seven analysts conducted by Reuters found a median forecast of A$85.7 million for GIO's net profit before abnormals and any transfer to its disaster reserve for the six months to December 31.
Analysts' forecasts varied widely with estimates ranging from A$80.0 million to A$95.7 million, with individual estimates grouped at both ends of the range.
The median estimate of A$85.7 million represents a 2.3 percent rise on the previous corresponding half year net result of A$83.8 million.

Bill Jocelyn, GIO's managing director has said the company would be disappointed if earnings for the 1996/97 year from its non-investment business units, which include its general insurance operations, did not match the previous year.

"On the business side ... I would be more than disappointed if we don't more than match last year's business results but overall for the group it depends on the returns from the investment side," he said after the annual meeting in November.

GIO's investment division is tipped to post strong earnings in the first half, but earnings from its insurance business is seen pressured by the stiff competition in the Australian market, analysts said.

"The result depends a lot on how well the investment division has done," an insurance analyst from a Sydney-based broker said. "There is the potential for the group to do much better than expected if it does well," the analyst said.
The company's 1995/96 results were adversely affected by losses arising from a market deterioration in Australian claims experience for motor vehicle insurance.
GIO's general insurance division recorded a loss of A$20.4 million in 1995/96 compared to a loss of A$29.8 million in the previous year.

On Monday, GIO peer QBE Insurance Group Ltd announced stronger first half earnings and said its result was aided by a better motor vehicle insurance market in New South Wales following changes to the legislation involving claims on Compulsory Third Party (CTP) insurance.
Analysts said GIO could make a transfer of A$8 million to its disaster reserve depending on the strength of its result.
GIO is at liberty to transfer any amount to its disaster reserve but previous transfers had typically amounted to A$8 million in any six month period.
